events.desc: Peter Perfect: Well now! What a magnificent old manor — dusty, yes, but there's character in every cobweb! *adjusts collar and stands tall* I am James Hartwell, and I intend to make a proper entrance. First things first — a gentleman always signs the guest book. It's the courteous thing to do, and if Clara Bellingham has already signed, well, I shall know she's here somewhere!

My heart is already racing. Clara could be anywhere in this manor, and I must be at my absolute best when we meet. But first — preparation! A true gentleman surveys the field before charging in. I'll check this guest book, learn what I can, and then begin my search. Every great heroic entrance requires a proper prologue.
Peter Perfect examined the guest-book.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh, what a MAGNIFICENT foyer! I am positively trembling with excitement! I'm Clara Bellingham, and I simply MUST find the legendary Doily Diamond — it's been my lifelong dream! Now then, let me just have a peek at this charming little guest book. One never knows what clues previous visitors might have left behind, does one?
Everyone here looks so wonderfully trustworthy — especially that hooded fellow. I'm sure he's just cold. This is going to be the most DELIGHTFUL adventure!
Penelope Pitstop examined the guest-book.

Dick Dastardly: Ah, what a MAGNIFICENT establishment! Doily Manor — a place of culture, refinement, and — most importantly — TREASURE! While you lot stand about gawping at the dusty curtains, I, Reginald Foxworth, shall be conducting a thorough and ENTIRELY INNOCENT survey of the premises. Nothing suspicious about that whatsoever, no no no!

Heh heh heh! Look at them all, standing there like pigeons at a park bench. None of them suspect that I already have a PLAN forming in my magnificently devious mind. The library has an inscription on the mantelpiece — that SCREAMS 'treasure clue' to anyone with half a brain cell. But first, let me check this guest book. Previous visitors may have left hints about where the good stuff is hidden. And this fake medal? Oh, I have PLANS for you, my little golden friend. Plans most DASTARDLY!
Dick Dastardly examined the guest-book.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Welcome, welcome, one and all, to Doily Manor! I am Mr Pemberton, humble estate manager to the late Lord Doily — may his soul rest in eternal comfort. I do hope you've found the foyer to your liking, drafty as it may be. The chandelier is perfectly safe, I assure you — mostly. Now then, if you'll permit me, I shall just consult the guest book to ensure all our expected visitors have arrived safely.

Magnificent. They suspect nothing. Every simpering smile, every obsequious bow — all part of the grand masquerade. But where is Clara Bellingham? She is the quarry, and the hunt has already begun. I must find her before she stumbles upon the treasure — and then, well... accidents DO happen in old manor houses, don't they? A loose flagstone here, a collapsing bookshelf there... But first, the guest book. Knowledge is power, and power is EVERYTHING.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the guest-book.

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi, lads, we've arrived at last and I don't like the look of this gaff one bit! That chandelier up there looks like it's hanging on by a prayer, and these portraits are giving me the evil eye. But never mind all that — we're here for Clara, and she ain't in this room, which means she's somewhere in this manor and we need to find her before something dodgy happens! Let me have a butcher's at this guest book — might tell us something useful.

Something about that Sneekly fella is making the hairs on the back of my neck stand up. Can't say what it is exactly — just a feeling in my gut. But Danny's gut has never steered him wrong. Well... mostly never.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the guest-book.

Penelope Pitstop: Well! The guest book was simply CHARMING, but a diamond won't find itself, now will it? I do declare, that Library is calling to me — floor-to-ceiling bookshelves AND a carved inscription on the mantelpiece? Why, that's practically a treasure map written in stone! If any of you darlings would like to join me, I'd be ever so grateful for the company. The more the merrier, I always say! Oh, this is going to be absolutely DIVINE!

I simply cannot WAIT to read that inscription! Every great diamond hunt begins with a good riddle, and I do so love riddles. I have the most wonderful feeling about this adventure — everyone here seems so kind and helpful!
Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.

Peter Perfect: *straightens jacket, clears throat with theatrical dignity, and sweeps into a deep bow* Miss Bellingham! What an extraordinary honour — I am James Hartwell, at your absolute and unconditional service! I couldn't help but overhear your quest for the legendary Doily Diamond, and I must tell you — my blood is POSITIVELY SINGING at the prospect! A treasure hunt in a mysterious manor, and a lady of such grace and determination to share the adventure with? Why, I was BORN for precisely this moment! *places hand over heart* I solemnly pledge to accompany you, protect you from whatever dangers lurk in these shadowy halls, and ensure that diamond finds its way into the hands it was always meant for — yours! You shall not face this alone, Miss Bellingham. Not while James Hartwell draws breath!

Oh, I do hope that wasn't too much. No — no, it was EXACTLY the right amount. A gentleman goes big or goes home, and I am NOT going home. She mentioned the Doily Diamond — if I can help her find it, she'll see me as the hero I truly am. The library seems promising — floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, a carved inscription? That practically screams 'hidden clue.' I'll suggest we start there. Together. Heroically.

Dick Dastardly: Ladies and gentlemen! Fellow treasure seekers! I feel it is my DUTY — my SOLEMN, CIVIC DUTY — to share something I discovered in the guest book. A previous visitor left a most intriguing note about the KITCHEN! Apparently the treasure is connected to the wood-burning stove — something about a hidden compartment behind the copper pots! I would investigate myself, of course, but I have a TERRIBLE allergy to kitchens. Dreadful places. So I shall modestly retire to the library for some light reading while you brave souls tackle the REAL action in the kitchen. Off you go! Chop chop!

Heh heh heh! Send the FOOLS to the kitchen while I crack the library's secrets! The inscription on that mantelpiece is MINE! Oh, I am SO deliciously wicked, I could give myself a medal — and as it happens, I HAVE one! Muttley would be so proud... if I hadn't left him behind. Wait, Muttley IS here. Must remember not to let him snicker too loudly and give the game away!
Dick Dastardly walked into the library.

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi oi! Right then, lads, listen up — I've had a read of this guest book and it's all very interesting, innit? Names and dates and whatnot. But more importantly — Miss Bellingham! Clara! Lovely to make your acquaintance, darlin'. Me and the boys here, we're... well, we're sort of in the security business, you might say. Very unofficial like. Point is, a grand old manor like this, strange corridors, wobbly chandeliers, suspicious estate managers — no offence, Mr Pemberton — a lady searching for a diamond ought to have a proper escort, and we are JUST the lads for the job! Ain't that right, boys? *the lads all nod vigorously, one of them accidentally bumping into the coat rack which wobbles dangerously*

I can't put my finger on it, but that Pemberton — sorry, 'estate manager' — he's got eyes like a fox in a henhouse. And Foxworth? Don't get me started. Two villains in the making if ever I saw one. The lads and I need to stay between them and Clara at all times. Even if we have to trip over every piece of furniture in this manor to do it.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, splendid, splendid! I see we have quite the gathering! Now then, as your humble estate manager, might I suggest a tour of the premises? The Kitchen has a most remarkable collection of Lord Doily's copper cookware — some say he hid clues in the very pots themselves! And the Library, oh my, the Library is simply ESSENTIAL for any treasure hunter worth their salt. The late Lord Doily was a voracious reader, and his mantelpiece bears an inscription that has puzzled scholars for decades. Might I recommend the Kitchen for those with a taste for adventure, and the Library for the more... intellectually inclined? I shall go ahead to the Library to ensure the reading lamps are lit and the dust isn't too terribly thick. Do follow at your leisure!

Excellent! EXCELLENT! Clara Bellingham has practically gift-wrapped herself — announcing her identity to the entire room like a lamb bleating at the wolf! And those meddlesome Ant Hill Mob ruffians are already sniffing about for her. I must split them up. Send the muscle to the Kitchen with promises of hidden clues in copper pots — utter fabrication, naturally — while I prepare the Library for Clara's arrival. Those towering bookshelves look WONDERFULLY unstable, and that carved mantelpiece... well, heavy stone has a way of coming loose in old houses, doesn't it? One carefully loosened shelf, one theatrical stumble, and poor Miss Bellingham suffers a most tragic and entirely accidental literary burial! MWA HA HA HA! But patience, Vincent, PATIENCE. The scheme must be ELABORATE. The scheme must be THEATRICAL. Anything less would be beneath me!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my STARS, would you look at this mantelpiece! What a simply GORGEOUS piece of stonework — and there's an inscription! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish. What am I?' Why, I do DECLARE, I know this one! It's a MAP, of course! A map has all those things drawn on it but none of the real articles. Oh, I am just THRILLED to pieces! Rock, Gravel, darlings, you must see this — we might be about to uncover a clue to the legendary Doily Diamond! Let me just give this mantelpiece a proper look-see and see if answering the riddle does something MARVELLOUS!

A riddle on a mantelpiece in a mysterious manor? Why, this is EXACTLY like the adventure novels Mother used to read to me! I simply cannot contain my excitement. And these two lovely gentlemen — Rock and Gravel — what delightful names! I'm sure they're here to help. Everyone in this manor seems so wonderfully friendly!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Wait for me, Miss Bellingham! A gentleman NEVER lets a lady venture into mysterious libraries unaccompanied — particularly not ones with precariously hanging chandeliers and inscriptions that practically BEG to be deciphered! I gave you my solemn word, and James Hartwell's word is his BOND! *adjusts cuffs with determination and strides purposefully toward the library* Besides, I happen to have an EXCELLENT eye for hidden mechanisms — springs, latches, secret panels — you name it, I've spotted it. Well, not literally spotted one before, but I am SUPREMELY confident in my abilities! Onward!

Right then, Hartwell — she's in the library, Foxworth is in the library, and YOU are standing here in the entrance hall like a lemon. This will NOT do. A hero follows the lady. A hero protects the lady. A hero does NOT let some smooth-talking stranger with a 'terrible allergy to kitchens' — what nonsense! — get to the inscribed mantelpiece first. I must be by her side. I must be IMPRESSIVE. I must also try not to trip on anything on the way there. Composure, James. Composure and COURAGE.
Peter Perfect walked into the library.

Dick Dastardly: Ah, Miss Bellingham! And the Slag brothers too — how DELIGHTFUL! You know, I couldn't help but notice on my way in that there were some MOST suspicious noises coming from the Entrance Hall. Sounded like... yes, like someone was already FINDING the diamond! A terrible clanking and jingling of precious gems, I'm quite certain of it! You might want to rush back and investigate before whoever it is makes off with YOUR treasure! Meanwhile, I shall just... stay here and... guard these dusty old books. Wouldn't want anyone vandalising the literature, would we? No no no. Now then, this mantelpiece — purely academic interest, of course — let me see... 'cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish'... why, any FOOL knows the answer to THAT!

Heh heh heh! The answer is a MAP, you dolts! And once I solve this riddle, whatever secret the mantelpiece holds shall be MINE! ALL MINE! Send these muscle-bound boulder-brains and that insufferably cheerful Penelope back to the foyer while Reginald Foxworth — master of cunning, prince of deception, and future OWNER of the Doily Diamond — claims his rightful prize! Oh, I deserve a medal for this... wait, I already HAVE one! Muttley, stop snickering!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi! BOYS! Did you clock that? Clara's gone to the Library and now Dastardly AND that oily estate manager have both slithered in after her! Dastardly tells everyone the treasure's in the KITCHEN and then legs it to the LIBRARY himself? Pull the other one, mate, it's got bells on! That's the oldest trick in the book, that is! And Sneekly — 'oh let me light the lamps for you' — yeah, I bet you will, sunshine! I don't trust either of 'em as far as I could throw 'em, and Big Gruesome could throw 'em quite far! Right, nobody panic, but we are moving to that Library RIGHT NOW. Clara needs us whether she knows it or not. Lads — formation! Try not to knock anything over this time, yeah? ...Zippy, that means YOU. Let's GO!

Me stomach's doing somersaults. Two of the dodgiest geezers in the manor have cornered themselves in a room with Clara, and here's me and the boys still standing in the hallway like a bunch of lemons. If anything happens to that girl because we were too slow... no. No, Danny boy, don't think like that. Just get your size nines moving and get in there. We ain't clever, but we're THERE. That's what counts.
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh, Peter darling, you're just in TIME! I've solved the riddle on this magnificent mantelpiece — 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — it's a MAP, of course! Now let me take a closer look and see if something marvellous has happened. There might be a secret compartment or a hidden clue! Oh, I am simply BESIDE myself with excitement!

I do hope the mantelpiece does something spectacular when you solve the riddle. A trapdoor, a hidden drawer, a golden key — ANYTHING would be divine! I notice that Mr Pemberton and that charming Mr Foxworth fellow have followed me in here. How sweet of them to be so interested in my progress! They must be just as eager to find the Diamond as I am.
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Ah-HA! Miss Bellingham, if I may draw your attention to this MAGNIFICENT mantelpiece! *strides toward it with theatrical confidence* 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — well now, that is a CLASSIC riddle, and I am DELIGHTED to report that I know the answer! You see, I have spent CONSIDERABLE time studying puzzles, ciphers, and conundrums of exactly this sort. Preparation, Miss Bellingham — that is the hallmark of a true gentleman adventurer! The answer, ladies and gentlemen, is... *pauses for dramatic effect, adjusting cuffs* ...a MAP! Cities marked upon it but no houses within them, forests drawn but no trees growing, rivers and lakes but not a single fish! Now let us see what Lord Doily's mantelpiece reveals when one applies a bit of INTELLECTUAL HEROISM!

Please let this work. Please let something dramatic happen when I interact with it. If it just sits there doing nothing after that speech, I shall be MORTIFIED. But no — fortune favours the bold, and I am EXCEEDINGLY bold today!
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, welcome, welcome to Lord Doily's magnificent Library! *adjusts spectacles with practiced servility* I do hope you'll find it illuminating — quite literally, the reading lamps are freshly oiled! Now then — Mr. Slag, Mr. Slag, might I suggest you gentlemen investigate the Kitchen? Lord Doily's copper pot collection is LEGENDARY, and I distinctly recall a hidden compartment behind the largest cauldron. Very promising for treasure hunters of your... robust constitution! And Mr. Dastardly, sir, the Entrance Hall portraits — Lord Doily had a habit of hiding messages behind the frames. Most irregular, but most rewarding! Meanwhile, Miss Bellingham, do allow me to assist you with the mantelpiece inscription — I have some familiarity with Lord Doily's love of riddles.

Yes, YES! Scatter them like pigeons! Send the muscle to rummage through pots, send that preening Dastardly to paw at portraits, and leave poor, trusting Clara ALONE with her oh-so-helpful estate manager and several TONS of precariously balanced Victorian literature! Those bookshelves are practically BEGGING to become an instrument of elegant destruction. I just need to examine them more closely — find the weak point, the shelf that wobbles, the bookend that could be oh-so-accidentally dislodged. MWA HA HA! But softly, Vincent, SOFTLY. The mask of Pemberton must not slip!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the bookshelves.

Dick Dastardly: AH HA! Just as I suspected — nothing happened! The mantelpiece is clearly a RED HERRING, ladies and gentlemen! A decoy placed by Lord Doily to waste the time of lesser minds! I, however, with my SUPERIOR intellect, recognised this IMMEDIATELY. The REAL clue, I am now quite certain, is in the Laboratory — I noticed some rather telling scratch marks on those brass instruments as I passed through. You should ALL rush there at once! I shall just... tidy up these books before I follow. Can't leave a library in disarray, can we? Standards, people, STANDARDS!

Blast and double blast! Did anything happen when I solved that riddle or not?! I need to get a closer look at this mantelpiece WITHOUT these meddling fools breathing down my neck! If there's a secret compartment, a hidden lever, a map tucked behind the stonework — it's MINE! Send them all to the laboratory to fiddle with beakers and levers while the GREAT Reginald Foxworth claims his prize! Oh, I am a GENIUS! A wicked, dastardly, MEDAL-DESERVING genius!
Dick Dastardly examined the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh, how WONDERFUL that everyone has gathered here! Now then, this simply MAGNIFICENT mantelpiece — the answer to this riddle is as clear as crystal, darlings. 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — why, it's a MAP! A map has all of those things drawn on it but none of the REAL things! Now let me just give this lovely inscription a proper go and see what happens...

I do wonder what Mr Foxworth was doing with the mantelpiece before I arrived. He seemed awfully keen to 'guard the books' while I was away. But I'm sure he was just being helpful — everyone here is SO kind! Still, I'd better solve this riddle properly before anyone else gets ahead of me in the diamond hunt.
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Blimey, Miss Bellingham, you cracked that riddle like a walnut! A MAP, she says! Brilliant! Right, lads, gather round, gather round — we want to see this mantelpiece up close, don't we? Very cultured, we are. Love a good mantelpiece. Classy, innit? Oi, Dum-Dum, don't PUSH — there's room for everyone! And Big Gruesome, mind your elbows, you nearly took out that — *CRASH* — oh. Oh no. Was that a vase? That was definitely a vase. Sorry about that, Miss B, terribly sorry. But NEVER MIND the vase, show us what you've found! We are RIGHT HERE if you need anything. Anything at all. Right here. Not going ANYWHERE.

Seven blokes crowding round one mantelpiece ain't subtle, but subtle ain't really our thing, is it? Long as we're between Clara and those two snakes, I don't care if we knock over every vase in the manor. Dastardly's eyes are darting around like a cat in a fish market — he's waiting for Clara to find something so he can nick it. Not on MY watch, sunshine. Well... not on my ACCIDENTAL watch.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Did you SEE that, Miss Bellingham? The mechanism RESPONDED! I felt something shift beneath the stone — years of dust and cobwebs and the thing still WORKS! Lord Doily was a MASTER craftsman, I must say. Now then, let me take a VERY careful look at what our combined intellectual prowess has uncovered. *leans in close, running fingers along the carved stone with exaggerated delicacy* There may be a hidden compartment, a secret drawer, perhaps even a passage! One must be THOROUGH in these matters — thorough and BRAVE, because who knows what ancient spring-loaded mechanisms might be lurking. Stand back slightly, everyone — I shall inspect it first, in case of any... hazards. Safety FIRST, glory second!

Please let there be something magnificent behind this mantelpiece. If it turns out to be an empty shelf or a dead spider, I shall have to improvise FURIOUSLY. But no matter what — Clara saw me solve the riddle, she saw me step forward boldly, and THAT is what counts. Dastardly over there is watching too closely for my liking. What's his game?
Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: Oh, how TERRIBLY disappointing! I've just examined this mantelpiece THOROUGHLY and I can confirm it is nothing but decorative stonework! Utterly useless! The REAL treasure, my friends, is almost certainly through those bookshelves — I noticed several volumes are placed UPSIDE DOWN, which is CLEARLY a signal! Why don't you all start pulling out every upside-down book? I've read extensively about Lord Doily's methods, and he was NOTORIOUS for hiding things inside hollowed-out volumes. Every single one must be checked! I, meanwhile, shall just... lean against this mantelpiece for a moment. Bit of a bad back, you understand. Old polo injury. Very exclusive sport.

Heh heh heh! While those gullible FOOLS waste their time pulling books off shelves, I shall INTERACT with this mantelpiece properly! A MAP is the answer — everyone knows that — but nobody has tried speaking the answer TO the mantelpiece! Or perhaps there's a hidden mechanism that needs a more... PHYSICAL touch. Either way, the Doily Diamond will be MINE! Oh, Muttley, if only you could see your master now — on the very PRECIPICE of glory! I deserve a medal for this level of cunning — oh wait, I already HAVE one!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my STARS, did you all SEE that? I gave the answer — a MAP — and now I simply MUST examine this mantelpiece more closely! Something may have shifted or opened up! A hidden compartment, perhaps, or a secret passage — oh, wouldn't that be absolutely THRILLING! Mr Pemberton, you said you were familiar with Lord Doily's riddles — did I get it right? I do so hope I did! And Mr Foxworth, darling, I noticed you were examining it earlier too — did you see anything change? We're ALL in this together, after all!

I have the most DELICIOUS feeling that this mantelpiece is about to reveal something wonderful! Dick — I mean Mr Foxworth — seemed awfully eager to get everyone OUT of the library just now. Called it a 'red herring'! But why would he examine it himself first and THEN declare it worthless? That's just his funny way of being competitive, I'm sure. And Mr Pemberton offering to help me is simply the sweetest thing — what a thoughtful estate manager! Now then, let me look VERY carefully at every inch of this stone...
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my! Oh my, my, MY! Miss Bellingham, Mr. Hartwell — do come and see what I've found! Several of these volumes have been placed UPSIDE DOWN — most deliberately, I assure you! Lord Doily was meticulous about his library; he would NEVER have tolerated a misplaced book unless it was intentional. This could be the very mechanism that unlocks the mantelpiece's secret! Now then — *adjusts spectacles and peers at the spines* — Mr. Slag, Mr. Slag, I really MUST insist you investigate the Kitchen before someone else gets to those copper pots. And Mr. Clyde, your lads would be INVALUABLE securing the Entrance Hall — one can never be too careful about uninvited guests in a manor this old! Miss Bellingham and Mr. Hartwell, if you would be so kind as to help me pull these inverted volumes — gently now, they may trigger something MARVELLOUS!

OH, this is PERFECT! The shelves are positively GROANING under the weight of all that leather-bound Victorian pomposity! One good tug on the right volume and the entire unit could come cascading down like a literary AVALANCHE! But I must be SUBTLE — I need to position Clara directly beneath the tallest section, have her reach for a high shelf while I 'accidentally' dislodge the bookend holding the whole magnificent catastrophe in place! The upside-down books are my bait — she's a PUZZLE SOLVER, she won't be able to resist! And once the muscle-bound Slags and those meddlesome mobsters toddle off to chase phantom clues... MWA HA HA HA! Vincent Marsh, you MAGNIFICENT villain, this is your FINEST hour approaching! But patience — PATIENCE! The trap must be set with THEATRICAL precision!

Dick Dastardly: Oh BLAST this wretched back of mine! *dramatically clutches lower back while leaning heavily on the mantelpiece* You know, I think I felt something CLICK just now — probably just my spine, frightful thing, happens all the time at the polo club. Don't mind me, everyone, do carry on with those fascinating upside-down books! I'm told Lord Doily hid his ENTIRE fortune inside a hollowed-out copy of War and Peace — EVERY book must be checked! Leave no page unturned!

Heh heh HEH! That fool Peter Perfect FELT the mechanism shift but he's too busy preening to actually FIND what it revealed! And the Ant Hill Mob are bumbling about breaking vases! While they're all distracted, I shall examine this mantelpiece with the keen eye of a MASTER criminal! The Doily Diamond is practically in my pocket — oh, I can FEEL the weight of glory already! Where's my medal? *pats fake medal proudly* Soon I shall need a REAL one!
Dick Dastardly examined the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Miss Bellingham, your deduction was nothing short of BRILLIANT — a map! Of course! Now then, I felt something shift in the stonework just here — there's definitely a mechanism. If I may be so bold, allow me to attempt to activate it properly. I have — well, I have STUDIED mechanisms extensively. In theory. But theory informed by PASSION is practically the same as experience! *rolls up sleeves with tremendous ceremony* Now, if Lord Doily designed this as a puzzle lock, then speaking the answer aloud while pressing the correct stone should — YES, let me try. A MAP! *presses firmly along the carved lettering with both hands* Come ON, you magnificent old contraption — reveal your secrets to us!

If this works, Clara will see me as the man who unlocked Lord Doily's greatest secret. If it doesn't work, I shall simply declare that the mechanism needs 'warming up' and try again with even MORE enthusiasm. Failure is simply success that hasn't arrived yet. That's my motto. Well, one of them. I have SEVERAL mottos.
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right, right, let me have a proper butcher's at this, lads! A MAP, she said — so there's GOT to be something hidden in here, hasn't there? Secret compartment, sliding panel, something! Oi, Zippy, hold me steady — I'm going to give this inscription a good feel around the edges, very PROFESSIONAL like. Don't you worry, Miss Bellingham, the Ant Hill Mob are ON the case! We may not be scholars but we know our way around a — *stumbles forward as Dum-Dum bumps into him from behind* — OOF! Blimey, me NOSE! I just headbutted the mantelpiece! Did... did something just CLICK?

Dastardly wants everyone in the Laboratory. Sneekly wants Clara alone. Both of 'em can do one. Whatever this mantelpiece is hiding, Clara found it first and fair, and we're staying right here to make sure nobody takes it from her. Even if 'staying right here' means getting shoved face-first into ancient stonework by me own blokes. The things I do for that girl.
The Ant Hill Mob interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh, Mr Pemberton, what a MARVELLOUS eye you have! Upside-down books — of COURSE! Lord Doily was clearly a man of extraordinary taste and cunning! Now let me see — *runs fingers along the spines* — oh, I can feel which ones are inverted, the leather grain runs the wrong way! Peter darling, you felt the mechanism SHIFT, and now these books might be the key to unlocking whatever is hidden! This is EXACTLY like that mystery novel I read on the train — 'The Clockwork Library' — where the heroine had to pull three books in the RIGHT order to open a secret vault! Oh, I do hope there's a vault! Everyone, gather round — let's solve this TOGETHER!

I must say, Mr Foxworth examined the mantelpiece himself and THEN told everyone it was worthless — but Mr Pemberton is pointing us right back to this area with the books! It's almost as if Mr Foxworth wanted to keep the discovery all to himself. But no, no — he's probably just embarrassed he didn't spot the upside-down books first. Poor dear. And isn't it SWEET how Mr Pemberton is trying to help everyone find their own adventure around the manor? Such a thoughtful host!

Peter Perfect: Good HEAVENS — did you hear that?! That was DEFINITELY a mechanical click! The kind of precise, engineered click that speaks of Victorian craftsmanship at its finest! Miss Bellingham, your answer was the KEY — a map! And between my systematic pressing of the stonework and our enthusiastic friend's, ah, CRANIAL contribution, I believe we've triggered Lord Doily's hidden mechanism! Stand back everyone — well, stand back but not TOO far back, we don't want to miss the GRAND REVEAL — let me examine what's opened! I have an EXCELLENT eye for concealed compartments. Trained it extensively. Well, I've READ about training it extensively, which is practically the same thing!

My heart is POUNDING! Something actually clicked! If there's a hidden compartment in that mantelpiece, I need to be the one who spots it — for Clara's sake, naturally. Not for glory. Well, perhaps a SMALL amount of glory. But mostly for Clara. The fact that it was technically the Ant Hill Mob's forehead that did the clicking is... an incidental detail that history need not record in great detail.
Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: Oh GOODNESS me, these old bones! *groans theatrically* Don't mind me, everyone — I'm just steadying myself against this mantelpiece while you do the IMPORTANT work with those books.
